To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“GPR43 and Gpr120 are up-regulated in a tissue specific manner by a high fat diet in rats.”
GPR43 and GRP120 are up-regulated in a tissue specific manner in response to a high fat diet.
diet-induced obesity up-regulates the abundance of GPR43 in liver and skeletal muscle and GPR120 gene abundance in cardiac and skeletal muscle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of insulin resistance and the metabolic syndrome.
the effect diet-induced obesity has on the expression of two fatty acid receptors (GPR43 and GPRO20) and the role they have in mediating metabolic processes in the liver, skeletal muscle and heart.
the role of GPR43, GPR120 and other receptors that recognise free fatty acids in the development of metabolic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the abundance of the receptors GPR43 and/or GPR120 is increased in a tissue specific manner in response to diet-induced obesity.
a HFD up-regulates GPR43 and/or GPR120 gene expression in tissues important in metabolic health.
GPR43 and/or GPR120 are up-regulated by HFD and that this is tissue specific.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GPR43 and 120 may have a role in mediating the metabolic dysfunction that is seen in obesity.
the GPR43 and/or GPR120 receptor may play an important role in regulating metabolic function in response to dietary fat.
GPR43 and 120 are up-regulated in response to diet-induced obesity in tissues important in regulating energy balance and glucose metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the upregulation of GPR receptors in response to a high fat diet is not uniform across all tissue types and that the GPR43 receptor may be a potential target for the treatment of metabolic disease.
GPR43 and GRP120 may be useful targets for the treatment of metabolic disorders such as obesity and type 2 diabetes.
GPR43 and/or GPR120 are likely to be important in the development of metabolic dysfunction in response to a high fat diet.
